title: Deferred Spec-Decoding Integration Gates and Rollback Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and integration guide for the deferred/speculative decoding path we want to land behind a feature gate. Focus: how the spec-decoder interacts with kernel selection, scheduler heuristics, and the KV cache; what signals we require for safe acceptance; and a concrete rollback plan if quality/regression or perf regressions show up in canary or early production traffic.

Context / problem statement:
- We introduced a speculative decode execution path that can start generating tokens using a looser kernel schedule and early kv prefetch. Goal is to reduce tail latency for common short-seq requests while maintaining correctness and cost efficiency.
- Risks: increased cache churn, stale KV reads for long-context requests, kernel misrouting for mixed-dtype quantized models, increased token-cost due to re-rolls when speculative outputs are discarded.

High-level integration gates (must pass all):
1) Functional correctness gate (local + unit tests):
   - deterministic fallback tests: when spec path is disabled, results match current mainline for a set of canonical prompts (score tolerance <= 1e-6 for logits, exact-match for tokenization where applicable).
   - KV recovery test: simulated eviction mid-generation must allow the mainline to recover without hangs.
2) Performance gate (synthetic and perf infra):
   - 95th pct token latency must be <= baseline 95th pct * 0.95 for short (<64 tokens) workload in LAB perf harness when spec path enabled.
   - Mean GPU utilization must not increase by >8% for same QPS in the lab.
3) Cost gate (estimation):
   - Token-per-second and effective cost per token projected from A/B run must not increase >5% for target workload.
4) Regression gate (quality):
   - Automated evals over production prompt set (sampled 2k prompts) must show no more than 0.5% relative degradation in model quality metrics used downstream (per-customer metric defined by product).
5) Observability gate:
   - Required labels/metrics emitted: spec_decode.enabled, spec_decode.reason, kvcache.prefetch_hit, kvcache.eviction_count, kernel.toggled, fallback_count. All must appear in the canary traces and be present in export pipeline.

Staging/canary rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: feature behind flag in staging only. Run end-to-end synthetic and smoke tests.
- Phase 1: 1% canary traffic from non-critical tenants (low QPS customers). Run for >=72h. Monitor baseline vs canary for: correctness, 95/99 latency, KV hit rate, fallback rate, and per-tenant request failure increase.
- Phase 2: 10% canary, include heavier workloads & mix of long-context. 72h.
- Phase 3: 50% selected regions/tenants. 48h.
- Phase 4: full ramp if metrics stable.

Must-have runtime flags / config knobs (for ops):
- spec_decode.enabled (global)
- spec_decode.cpu_fallback_threshold_ms (if kernel fallback takes longer than X ms, prefer non-spec path)
- spec_decode.max_unacked_prefix_tokens (to limit how much speculative work we may discard)
- kvcache.prefetch_window_tokens (how many future KV entries to prefetch)
- kernel.routing.score_threshold (for routing to specialized kernels vs generic kernel)

Key metrics and alert conditions (automatic alarms):
- spec_decode.fallback_rate > 0.75% sustained over 10m => P1 alert. High fallback rates indicate spec path is misaligned with workload.
- kvcache.hit_rate drop > 6% vs baseline 30m rolling => investigate eviction policy or prefetch adverse effects.
- tail_latency_95 increase > 7% vs baseline 30m rolling => P1 on-call.
- token_waste_rate (speculative tokens discarded / total tokens generated) > 4% => ops review.
- correctness_regressions: weekly automated eval count of failed cases increases by >1% relative.

KV cache considerations (detailed):
- Prefetch semantics: prefetch should only populate ephemeral KV shards tied to the spec session id. These ephemeral entries must have a TTL equal to spec_decode.ephemeral_ttl_ms (default 30s) and be marked as lower-priority for eviction.
- Eviction policy: introduce a two-tier eviction queue: ephemeral-prefetch tier + persistent tier. Eviction from ephemeral tier should be LRU within ephemeral entries and never force-evict pinned persistent entries.
- Staleness handling: if a generation spans >prefetch_window_tokens and cache entries evicted, the runtime must detect missing KV sequences and fall back to full rehydration path (non-spec).
- Metrics: emit kvcache.prefetch_hit, kvcache.prefetch_miss_reason (evicted|not-fetchable|open-io-error), kvcache.ephemeral_count.

Kernel routing and scheduling interactions:
- Kernel selection heuristics must be extended to consider "speculative" affinity: if request flagged spec_decode, prefer low-latency kernel implementations (FP16 fused ops, small-batch optimized kernels). For large-seq or when kv staleness detected, switch to throughput-optimized kernels.
- Scheduling: scheduler should apply a soft cap for speculative tasks to limit burst of small jobs stealing capacity from long-context batches. Implement a weighted round-robin where spec jobs carry lower weight and are allowed to preempt only a fraction of the queue.
- Telemetry hooks: each kernel invocation should log kernel.id, kernel.version, requested_dtype, batch_size, and spec_flag to enable offline analysis of kernel routing decisions.

Acceptance test matrix (minimal list to add to CI):
- unit: spec decode path returns same token sequence for 100 canonical prompts when prefetch disabled (fast asserts).
- integration: 72h perf harness run comparing spec-enabled vs disabled across short/long mixes.
- chaos test: kill GPU mid-session to ensure fallback and KV rehydrate path kicks in within 5s.
- regression: run downstream eval suite (narrative QA, summarization) and check for metric drift.

Rollback plan (fast and safe):
1) Immediate kill: flip spec_decode.enabled=false at the global control plane. This should be a single API call; ensure playbook on-call has runbook.
2) If kill causes secondary issues (e.g., unexpected latency spike due to removal of prefetch): rollback kernel routing change separately by setting kernel.routing.spec_affinity=false.
3) If metrics indicate cache contamination (persistent eviction of hot keys), restore persistent cache pinning config and flush ephemeral cache only (kvcache.flush_ephemeral=true).
4) Post-rollback forensic steps: download traces for the last 4 hours across canary tenants, collect fallback_count, prefetch_miss_reason, kernel.version, and submit a postmortem.

Open questions / TODOs (things to resolve before GA):
- Should ephemeral-prefetch entries be visible to cross-request reuse when the same tenant issues related requests within ephemeral_ttl? (pros: hit rate boost; cons: potential leakage). Need legal/security review.
- Define exact threshold for token_waste_rate that is tolerable per-customer SLAs.
- Kernel selection: should we add a machine-learning based router later to predict which kernel will minimize end-to-end latency? Track as a follow-up RFC.
- Cost analytics: add model-level per-token accounting for speculative wasted tokens to billing exports for pilot tenants.

Appendix: Quick command cheat-sheet (ops)
- Enable canary: POST /control/flags spec_decode.enabled=true scope=canary-ids
- Rollback: POST /control/flags spec_decode.enabled=false scope=global
- Flush ephemeral: POST /kvcache/flush?type=ephemeral
- Inspect metrics: /dashboards/spec-decode-canary?range=24h

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive; most of the gating thresholds are conservative to avoid noisy rollouts. Please add concrete dataset names for the production evals and any tenant exceptions you recommend.
- If we accept this, next steps are: add CI integration tests for KV eviction injection, add the metrics to the export pipeline, and schedule a 72h staged canary run with product/CS-observed prompts.

Unresolved items logged as tickets: ENG-1310 (ephemeral cache security review), ENG-1312 (billing for speculative tokens), ENG-1313 (kernel-routing heuristics RFC).

-- end of doc --
